Captures often arrive packed: a `.tgz` of a ring buffer, a password-protected
ZIP from a carrier, a 7z from an incident-response team. Point `-I` at the
archive and sipnab reads every capture inside, in capture order, as if you had
unpacked it into a directory. It leaves no decrypted copy behind.

## Before you start

- **A build with `archive`** for ZIP and 7z. Every release binary and package
  has it, the static musl tarballs and the `-noaudio` packages included. Check
  that `archive` is in the `features:` list of `sipnab --version`. tar, `.tgz`
  and gzip need no feature.
- **No privileges.** Reading an archive is reading a file.
- **No change on any other system.** sipnab reads the archive as it arrived.

What ran: every command and output on this page ran on 2026-11-03 with sipnab
0.5.232 built from source. GNU tar, Info-ZIP `zip -e` and 7-Zip 25.01
(`7z a -tzip -mem=AES256`, `7z a -mhe=on`) made the archives from two captures:
`sample-call.pcap` (see [Triage a capture from the command
line](@/docs/first-cli-triage.md)) and a second one-call capture, `sip-call.pcap`.

## Read a tar or a `.tgz`

```bash
sipnab -N -I session.tgz --report --no-cli-print
```

Read the lines sipnab prints before the report. They account for every member:

```text
WARN sipnab::capture::input_set: Skipping 'session.tgz/notes.txt': not a capture (starts with 63 61 6c 6c, which is not pcap or pcapng)
WARN sipnab::capture::input_set: Skipping 'session.tgz/evidence.zip/sample-call.pcap': encrypted, and no password was supplied (--archive-password-file, --archive-password-command, --archive-password-stdin, or the prompt)
WARN sipnab::capture::input_set: Skipping 'session.tgz/evidence.zip/sip-call.pcap': encrypted, and no password was supplied (--archive-password-file, --archive-password-command, --archive-password-stdin, or the prompt)
INFO sipnab::capture::input_set: 'session.tgz' unpacked (gzip > tar > gzip): 2 capture(s) to read, 3 member(s) not read, 1 directory entr(ies)
WARN sipnab::capture::input_set: -I resolved to 2 capture file(s), 3 archive member(s) not read (each named above with its reason)
```

This archive held a ring buffer of two captures, one of them gzip-compressed, a
text note, and a password-protected ZIP:

- The two captures joined the set, and sipnab read them in capture order,
  whatever their names.
- `gzip > tar > gzip` names the layers sipnab unwrapped, outermost first. It
  goes up to four layers deep and recognizes each by its bytes, not its name.
- sipnab names the note and the locked ZIP's members with the reason it did
  not read them. The run went on with the rest.
- `--input-name` reads only the members whose file name matches, as it does in
  a directory: `--input-name 'a.pcap'`.

## Read a password-protected ZIP or 7z

Give sipnab the password, and it reads the members as it reads a tar's. Keep
the password off the command line: this section lists the sources best first.

### From a file

The file holds one password per line. sipnab refuses a file that other users
can read:

```bash
sipnab -N -I evidence.zip --archive-password-file pcaps.pw --report --no-cli-print
```

```text
--archive-password-file 'pcaps.pw' can be read or written by other users (mode 0644); chmod 600 it
```

That run exited `2`. After `chmod 600 pcaps.pw`, the same command read both
members:

```text
INFO sipnab::privilege: Core dumps disabled (decryption active)
INFO sipnab::capture::input_set: 'evidence.zip' unpacked (zip): 2 capture(s) to read, 0 member(s) not read, 0 directory entr(ies)
INFO sipnab::app::batch: sipnab: 640 packets captured, 40 SIP messages, 600 RTP packets across 2 streams
```

sipnab accepts a file another user owns, such as a Kubernetes secret mount.
`--archive-password-file <(pass show pcaps/lab)` keeps the password off the
disk.

### From a password manager

sipnab runs the command without a shell and uses the first line it prints:

```bash
sipnab -N -I evidence.7z --archive-password-command 'pass show pcaps/lab' --report --no-cli-print
```

A run whose command printed the 7z's password read both members:

```text
INFO sipnab::capture::input_set: 'evidence.7z' unpacked (7z): 2 capture(s) to read, 0 member(s) not read, 0 directory entr(ies)
```

### From stdin, for a CI job

```bash
printf '%s\n' "$PCAP_PW" | sipnab -N -I evidence.zip --archive-password-stdin --report --no-cli-print
```

### From a systemd credential, for a service

When `$CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY/archive-password` exists, sipnab reads it as a
password file. In a unit, that is one line:

```ini
LoadCredential=archive-password:/etc/sipnab/pcaps.pw
```

The same setting on a transient unit read the ZIP with no password flag at
all:

```bash
systemd-run --user --wait --pipe -p LoadCredential=archive-password:/etc/sipnab/pcaps.pw \
  sipnab -N -I /srv/captures/evidence.zip --no-password-prompt --report --no-cli-print
```

```text
INFO sipnab::capture::input_set: '/srv/captures/evidence.zip' unpacked (zip): 2 capture(s) to read, 0 member(s) not read, 0 directory entr(ies)
```

### From the environment, or the command line

`SIPNAB_ARCHIVE_PASSWORD` works, but every child process inherits it.
`--archive-password` works too, and sipnab warns on every use, because other
users can read it in `ps`:

```text
WARN sipnab::capture::archive::password: WARNING! Using --archive-password on the command line is insecure: other local users can read it in `ps`, and it is saved in shell history. Use --archive-password-stdin, --archive-password-file or --archive-password-command.
```

### At the terminal

With no password configured, or none that opens a member, sipnab asks on the
terminal, three times per archive:

```bash
sipnab -N -I evidence.7z --report --no-cli-print
```

```text
Password for evidence.7z (member (the archive), attempt 1 of 3):
Wrong password. Password for evidence.7z (member (the archive), attempt 2 of 3):
```

- It reads `/dev/tty`, so it asks even with stdin redirected, and echoes
  nothing.
- An empty entry skips that archive's locked members. Ctrl-C stops the run
  with exit `130`.
- A 7z made with `-mhe=on` encrypts its member list too, so the prompt names
  the archive rather than a member.
- With no terminal (cron, CI, an agent), or with `--no-password-prompt`,
  sipnab never asks and never waits.
- The TUI asks in a popup instead
  ([Archive password popup](@/docs/keybindings.md#archive-password-popup)).

### Over REST

A client of the REST API's capture comparison may send a password for one
request in a header. sipnab accepts it from a client on the same host only,
unless you start sipnab with `--api-accept-archive-passwords`:

```bash
printf 'Sipnab-Archive-Password: %s\n' "$(pass show pcaps/lab)" \
  | curl -s -H @- "http://127.0.0.1:18080/v1/captures/compare?a=evidence.zip&b=sample-call.pcap" | jq .a
```

```json
{"filename":"evidence.zip","packets":640,"dialogs":8,"streams":2,"dialogs_dropped":0}
```

Without the header, the same request answered that the archive had no readable
capture, naming each member `encrypted_no_password`.
[`GET /v1/captures/compare`](@/docs/api.md#get-v1-captures-compare) gives the
rules. MCP takes no archive password on any tool: an agent's
`open_capture` uses the passwords the operator configured.

## Check that it worked

- The `unpacked` line counts what sipnab reads and what it does not.
- Every member it did not read has its own `Skipping` line.
- A run that read nothing from an archive named with `-I` exits `1`, naming
  each member with its reason code:

  ```text
  -I/--input: cannot read capture 'evidence.7z' named with -I: no readable capture in it (evidence.7z: encrypted_wrong_password)
  ```

- A run that read some members exits `0`. The closing `-I resolved to` line
  counts the rest.

## When something does not work

| What sipnab says | Why | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| `encrypted, and no password was supplied` | No source gave a password, and there was no terminal to ask on | Add `--archive-password-file` or another source |
| `encrypted, and no password supplied opens it` | Every password tried was wrong | Check the password. For a ZIP from an old Windows tool, try `--archive-password-encoding cp437` |
| `can be read or written by other users (mode 0644); chmod 600 it`, exit 2 | The password file is not private | `chmod 600` it |
| `uses ZipCrypto, which does not protect its contents` | The ZIP uses the legacy cipher (Info-ZIP's `zip -e` does) | sipnab reads it. Ask the sender to re-encrypt with AES-256 |
| `xz data, which sipnab does not unwrap` (or `zstd`, `bzip2`, `LZ4`) | A compression sipnab does not read | Unpack that member with its own tool, then point `-I` at the result |
| `decompressing reached the N-byte ceiling` | The archive inflates past `--max-gunzip-bytes` (1 GiB) | For an archive you trust, raise it |
| `could not be read past this point`, `INCOMPLETE RUN`, exit 1 | The archive stops early | sipnab kept what arrived. Fetch the archive again |
| `has link type N, which sipnab does not decode` | A member is not an IP capture, such as an LTE MAC log | Nothing: its frames count as not decoded |

[Archives](@/docs/cli.md#archives) and [Archives read like
directories](@/docs/cli.md#archives-read-like-directories) give every rule:
nesting, member names, ceilings, and where the unpacked copies live while a run
reads them.
